title: Play probe snapshot
description: What a built game reports about itself while it runs, so it can be played and judged from outside: `window.__wgf__.play.snapshot()` returns one object of this shape. The game installs it (the template installs `window.__wgf__`; the game adds `play`). It is read-only: calling it never changes the game. The playability step drives the game with real input and reads a snapshot before and after each input; it never acts through the probe. Metric names are the ones the design's `build_spec.experience` and `hud[].metric` use, so a snapshot can be held to the design. `audio` (optional) reports the music playing and the measured output level. `oracle` is present only when the page URL carries `wgf-probe=1`: a shipped build never computes it, and a release refuses a build that would. Optional beside `snapshot()`, and only with `wgf-probe=1`: `play.showcase`, an object with `targets()` - the runtime asset ids of readable entities this build can stage, typically those that first appear after the opening unit - and `show(assetId)` - puts the running game into a real state of play in which an entity drawn from that asset is on screen (the unit it first appears in, its encounter), resolving true, or false when it cannot. The bot calls it only in a test of its own, after the fresh-save tests, to capture a frame of each staged state for the production gate, which credits an asset there only where the frame shows it; it is never used to play, and a game without it is judged as before. Optional too, and only with `wgf-probe=1`: the unit link - a page URL that also carries `wgf-unit=<unit id>` (a build_spec.content.units id) starts play in that unit, as a level select would, so the content-sufficiency step's survey can measure every unit a build carries, not only the first few the bot plays to in order; a build that cannot enter a unit that way starts as it otherwise would, and the survey records the unit as not entered. While a content unit is in play (`content.unit_id` is a string), every entity of a content role - threat, goal, target, projectile, collectible, hazard - carries its `kind`: kinds are how the build shows which element is on screen, and without them element variety cannot be counted on the build (required with the content-sufficiency step; both validation builds of 2026-10 lacked them).

state.description: The session state, in these words whatever the game calls them. `won` and `lost` are the ends of play the experience contract names; a result screen after either keeps reporting it until play starts again.

metrics.description: Every metric the design's experience contract relies on (the goal's, win's, lose's, and every metric an action updates), by the same name, at its current value. Recommended keys beyond those, so a run can be judged against the design's content contract: `unit` - the current unit's index, 1-based; `best` - the best the player has reached, when the design persists one; `difficulty.<axis>` - the value in force now on each axis the design declares in build_spec.difficulty.axes, one key per axis, so a bot can see difficulty actually move; and every metric the design says persists between sessions, at the value just loaded.

content.description: Where in the game's content the player is now: which unit (level, wave, track, encounter, scenario, round) of how many, what it asks for, and how far through it they are. A game with units reports it so a bot can play several of them and a check can tell that the units differ; `unit_id` is null before play starts or between units. Units are the design's (build_spec.content.units), by id and in its order.

unit_id.description: The build_spec.content.units id of the unit in play, or null when none is.

unit_index.description: Its place in the sequence, 1-based; 0 when no unit is in play.

unit_count.description: How many units the build carries. For procedural content, how many a session is designed to meet.

unit_kind.description: What a unit is called here - level, wave, track, lap, encounter, scenario, shift, round, map, run-segment.

objective.description: The unit's objective, in the words the player is shown.

progress.description: How far through the unit the player is, on the unit's own measure. `value` rises toward `target` and the unit's objective is met when value >= target (gems 2 of 3, waves cleared 4 of 5, goal reached 0 of 1): never a count that falls (moves left, time left) - that is a lose metric, reported in metrics.

metric.description: The metric progress is counted in, named as `metrics` names it.

target.description: The value that completes the unit.

entities.description: The things on screen a player must be able to see, with where they are drawn now.

inputs.description: Every input the player can make right now, each as the control action it performs and the real input that performs it.

assets_loaded.description: Runtime asset ids (public/assets/assets.json) the game has loaded so far.

audio.description: What the game's audio is doing now. Optional, and additive: a game with sound reports it so the production gate can hear it play (audio.plays) and fall silent when muted. `level` is measured, not declared: the RMS of the game's master output (linear, 0-1) over the last few tens of milliseconds, read from an AnalyserNode placed after every gain the game applies - mute, pause, an ad break - so it is about 0 whenever the player hears nothing.

music.description: The runtime asset id of the music playing now (the main track of a layered one), or null.

playing.description: Music is playing and audible now: started, its context running, and not muted, paused or held for an ad.

level.description: Measured RMS of the master output, 0-1 (linear; 0.01 is -40 dBFS).

muted.description: The game holds its sound off now: the player's toggle, the platform's mute or an ad, a pause, or no input yet.

oracle.description: Only with `wgf-probe=1` in the URL: the input that succeeds now (a save, a match, a dodge), or null when no input matters now. Lets the playability step reach `won` and play badly on purpose to reach `lost`. Across units: when a unit has ended in success, the oracle names the input that advances to the next one (the `next` or `continue` control action), so a bot can play unit after unit with real input. It never names an input that skips a unit the player has not finished, and the bot never jumps to one while it plays: it plays every unit it reports. (The optional `play.showcase` stages states only for the production gate's frames; no unit is played or judged through it.)

kind.description: What the game itself calls this thing - `swarmer`, `turret`, `ice-tile`, `boost-pad`. Free text, and the game's own vocabulary; `role` stays the fixed one the checks read. A check counting distinct kinds in a unit (a wave with one enemy kind is not a composition) counts these. Required of every entity of a content role while a content unit is in play (the root `allOf`).

role.description: What the entity is to the player. The visual gate requires every player, threat, goal, target and projectile entity to be on screen and large enough to read.

x.description: Left edge of its drawn bounds, CSS px from the viewport's left.

y.description: Top edge, CSS px from the viewport's top.

visible.description: Drawn this frame: not hidden, culled, fully transparent or behind another opaque object.

asset.description: The runtime asset id (public/assets/assets.json) that draws it; null when nothing from the manifest does.

render.description: How it is drawn: from a manifest asset, as an engine primitive (a box, sphere, capsule, plain rectangle or circle), as text, or as several assets together. A greybox draws primitives; production draws readable entities from assets unless the design's visual_identity.primitive_style says otherwise.

x.description: CSS px from the viewport's left.

hold_ms.description: How long the input is held down: for a control that acts while held (steer, charge). Absent: a tap or a key press.

key.description: A KeyboardEvent.key value, e.g. ArrowLeft or ' '.

hold_ms.description: How long the input is held down: for a control that acts while held (steer, charge). Absent: a tap or a key press.
